producer_report.summary: Root cause: the baseline kept one pass/fail bit per check name. `Baseline::failed_before` matched by name and `verify::is_pre_existing` used it, with no per-test comparison. A check that failed on the base therefore excused every failure inside it, including a different new failing test. Fix at that comparison: `CheckRun.failed_tests` (optional, skipped when empty, so older records still parse and serialise as before) is filled by `run_check`, which makes both the baseline runs and the candidate runs. `checks::failed_test_names` reads cargo's `failures:` lists per test binary as `<binary> <test>` (`doc-tests <crate> <test>` for doc tests). A binary with no `test result:` line, or whose listed count differs from its failed count, is recorded as `<binary> (did not finish)`, so a crash counts as new. For a plain `cargo test`, `cargo_test_args` adds `--no-fail-fast` so every binary runs. The recorded `command` stays as configured and a failed run's `note` says the flag was added. `is_pre_existing` now excuses a failing check only when every failing test also failed on the base; if either side has no names, the check-name rule stands. `judge` adds one Minor finding that separates newly failing tests from tests already failing on the base. The `check X failed` reason is unchanged, so a failure counts once. Scope: this covers a different test failing inside a check that already failed on the base. A clash with a concurrent config or test change is NOT separated, because the baseline runs on the job's fixed base. CHANGELOG and the design note say so. Docs and comments updated in CHANGELOG.md, docs/design/job-planning.md, run/checks.rs and run/verification.rs. Eight one-line `failed_tests: Vec::new()` additions were compile-forced in other files.

open_issues: Case (b), a failure from a clash with a concurrent config or test change, is not separated: the baseline runs on the job's fixed base, and rebasing or merging concurrent changes is out of scope. The CHANGELOG and the design note say so.

When the base failed with test names and the candidate's check fails with none (build error, timeout, kill), the check-name rule still excuses it. A stricter rule would change `held_for_timeout` and is left out.
A base that failed with no names (build error) still excuses a candidate that now has test failures, as before.
A test check that is not a plain `cargo test` (wrapper script, nextest, `cargo +toolchain test`) records no names and keeps the check-name rule.

The real athena.toml test command was not inspected for this change. If it is not a plain `cargo test`, no names are recorded and the check-name rule stays.
mistakes: My first `run_check` edit collected redacted names with `collect::<Result<Vec<_>>>()`, which did not compile because `redact` returns a `GateError`. Replaced with a loop.
A first test used `&[crashed.clone()]`, which clippy rejected; fixed with `std::slice::from_ref`.

I could not read the large `cargo test -p athena-core -p athena-cli` output, since it was saved outside the working directory and Grep refused it. I relied on the clean exit status; the targeted runs earlier were read in full.
learnings: `CheckRun` has `deny_unknown_fields`, and a new `#[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Vec::is_empty")]` field keeps old records parsing and unchanged records byte-identical.
`run_check` is the only producer of both baseline runs (via `baseline_runs`) and candidate runs, so one field and one parser serve both sides.
`check_record_file` returns `Result<Option<AnyRecord>, RecordError>`; use `AnyRecord::parse` to get the record.
`Redactor::redact` returns a `GateError` result, so `.collect::<Result<Vec<_>>>()` into anyhow does not compile; a plain loop with `?` does.
Clippy denies `&[x.clone()]` for a slice from a reference in tests (`cloned_ref_to_slice_refs`); use `std::slice::from_ref`.
Bash in this environment allows only cargo, git status/diff/log/show, ls, mv, rm and chmod; grep and tail are refused, and tool results saved outside the working directory cannot be read with Grep.
desires: A way to read large saved tool output inside the working directory, or Bash `tail` and `grep` for command output.
